title: Opportunity Solution Tree Canvas
description: Teresa Torres OST — opportunities discovered through user research. Each opportunity entry requires provenance to prevent the canvas from drifting toward confident speculation (dogfood T4).

desired_outcome.description: The tree root. SINGULAR — retained as the default and only root for the common case. When a project needs more than one root, use `desired_outcomes` instead; declaring both is an error caught by validate_canvas.py.

desired_outcomes.description: MULTIPLE TREE ROOTS in one file, added v0.93.0. An OST rooted on a metric the project does not steer by will faithfully optimise the wrong thing — the tree stays busy while the stuck thing stays stuck. Splitting into a second FILE was the obvious move and is wrong twice over: the ID references that point into this canvas break, and the new file is read by no script, gate or render, which is the built-not-wired defect this framework audits for. So roots are declared here and opportunities name theirs via `rolls_up_to`, keeping every reference intact and every consumer working.

north_star_input_ref.description: Which north-star input metric this root feeds, or the literal `off_north_star` when it deliberately serves none. Naming it explicitly is the point: an unlabelled root reads as on-strategy by default.

review_by.description: REQUIRED IN PRACTICE when north_star_input_ref is `off_north_star` (validate_canvas reports its absence, v0.217.0): the date by which this root is resolved into an outcome or retired. check_target_progress reports it once passed. A root that serves no outcome and has no date is a parking lot with a label; the label is read (ost-render shows it), and what it licensed on the dogfood canvas was 58 of 73 opportunities parked for months.

review_condition.description: What would resolve or retire this off-outcome root: the outcome it is expected to serve once named, or the state in which its entries are re-homed. Required beside review_by for an `off_north_star` root.

cynefin_domain.description: Cynefin domain. Drives METHOD selection (clear=best practice, complicated=expert analysis, complex=probe-sense-respond, chaotic=act-sense-respond, confused=stop and establish which domain you are in), so a stale classification routes real work through the wrong method. v0.242.0 added `cynefin_classified_at` and `cynefin_basis` as siblings: until then this was a bare enum with no timestamp and no evidence reference, so it could not be known to be stale and could not be traced to what it rested on. A classification made on early evidence and never revisited is the defect; the sibling fields are what make it detectable.

sub_opportunities.description: Children of this opportunity (v0.207.0; a bare array with no reader from v0.1 until then). Two item shapes: a string is the id of a sibling opportunity in this file and must resolve (validate_canvas warns when it does not); an object is an inline sub-case that is not a node of its own and must carry id and name. ost-builder writes it; ost-render does not walk it yet, and the ost-builder skill says so.

solutions.description: Solution leaves under this opportunity. Items were untyped until v0.203.0, which is how `evidence_type: research` passed on five leaves (dogfood 2026-09-10). Only the declared keys are constrained; everything else a leaf carries is still allowed.

provenance.description: Solution-leaf provenance. Deliberately NOT the strict `_common` provenance object: leaves carry extra provenance keys in practice (blind_review, n_events, retrofit_note on the dogfood canvas, 2026-09-14), and the point of v0.203.0 is the ladder enum, not a key whitelist.

shipped_at.description: ISO date the leaf shipped. A field, so the outcome-check lag and cycle-history can read it instead of inferring the date from prose (v0.203.0).

minted_by.description: The skill or surface that minted the leaf (e.g. /mycelium:ost-builder, a scout harvest, a founder ruling). Provenance as a field, not prose (v0.203.0).

purpose_stance.description: Per-property stance of this leaf against purpose_properties (docs/purpose-stance.md). Keys are pp-NNN ids mapping to {verdict, note, override?}; a few meta keys sit beside them. written_by (v0.207.0) says who authored the block — the agent or a human — which confirmed_by alone cannot tell you: absent confirmation is not evidence of agent authorship.

status.description: Lifecycle state. Was an undeclared extra property until v0.86.0, which is how one dogfood canvas drifted to five spellings including an uppercase variant no validator could see.

closure_reason.description: Why this was closed. Must name what happened, not how long it has been.

reopen_trigger.description: What would make this closure wrong, stated concretely enough to be checked by someone who was not there. This is the field that turns a stale closure into a detectable one.

rolls_up_to.description: Which declared root in `desired_outcomes` this opportunity serves. Required on every opportunity once a file declares multiple roots — an untagged opportunity in a multi-root tree has no defined parent, and silently defaulting it to the first root is how the wrong-root problem returns. Ignored, and unnecessary, in a single-root file.

cynefin_classified_at.description: ISO date the domain was classified. REQUIRED IN PRACTICE once cynefin_domain is set: without it the classification cannot be compared against evidence that landed later, and check_cynefin_freshness reports it as UNCHECKABLE rather than fresh. Absent is not the same as current.

cynefin_basis.description: One line naming what the classification rested on — the evidence, the uncertainty, or the reason a domain was chosen. A domain with no basis cannot be re-argued when the data changes; the next reader can only accept or discard it.
